messages:
Maya Chen: Quick post-analysis from last night's regional spike — recording notes and action items here. TL;DR: routing preference + quota bump to a single EU AZ caused localized GPU pressure, KV cache thrash, and burst throttling.
Luca Patel: Thanks — can you share the sequence?
Maya Chen: Timeline: 21:03 service-level rollout (config change) set routing policy to prefer eu-west-1 for cheaper instances, 21:07 outbound traffic replay (promo) started, 21:10 autoscaler hit cold-start limit for other regions, 21:11 sustained queue growth on eu-west-1 dedicated pool -> OOM-near events.
Sam O'Neill: Observed symptom was continuous prefill and high kv-cache eviction rates, right?
Maya Chen: Exactly. Metrics: node GPU util peaked at 96-99%, KV cache eviction rate jumped x12, and per-request latency tail rose from 180ms to ~2.1s for cached routes.
Infra Bot: Deploy: routing-preference:v2 -> applied by infra-deploy-bot at 2025-11-14T21:03:12Z :white_check_mark:
Luca Patel: Why didn't autoscaler rebalance to other regions? We have policy to spill to us-west on saturation.
Maya Chen: The autoscaler has a safety threshold that prevents cross-region reallocation when predicted cold-start > 45s (we use conservative penalty for inter-region warmups). With the sudden promo surge, the predictor flagged high warmup risk and we fell back to throttling rather than spillover.
Sam O'Neill: So policy + cost-preference combo caused hot-spotting. Any networking factors?
Maya Chen: There was an additional subtlety: the new routing policy used prioritized endpoints list that ranked eu-west-1 endpoints by price and then by latency. Because of a recent price change, eu-west-1 got an elevated rank and got most of the traffic even though capacity delta was small.
Ops Lead: That prioritized list is supposed to be weight-balanced. Looks like weight normalization didn't kick in after the price update.
Luca Patel: We also saw TCP retransmits between the control-plane and eu-west-1 agent during the hottest 6 minutes — likely increased churn due to pressure.
Maya Chen: I pulled the agent logs:
```
2025-11-14T21:09:24Z agent[euw1-rtg]: kv_cache_evictions=1345 per_min, available_gpu_memory=430MiB
2025-11-14T21:10:01Z scheduler: enqueue_delay_ms=4800 pending_reqs=420
2025-11-14T21:10:40Z k8s: pod_restart_count=12 node_pressure=memory
```
Sam O'Neill: OOM-near events were transient; most pods didn't fully OOM but CPU/GPU contention forced latency-based shedding.
Nora (Finance): Rough cost impact? We turned on extra dedicated units for 15 minutes.
Maya Chen: Preliminary estimate: extra reserved and on-demand failover during the incident added ~1,100 GPU-hours equivalent to our usual day rate because of over-provisioning in eu-west-1 and failed spill. Estimated incremental cost: $9.2k (gross).
Nora (Finance): Oof. Need mitigations to avoid both customer latency and runaway cost.
Luca Patel: Root causes: 1) routing preference update prioritized single region after price rebalance, 2) autoscaler safety heuristic prevented cross-region spill because of conservative warmup penalty, 3) a weight normalization bug meant endpoint weights weren't rebalanced, 4) telemetry blind spot for per-route token cost and prefix cache hit rates.
Maya Chen: Agreed. Lessons: - Don't let price-only ranking alone drive routing decisions; use combined capacity score (capacity headroom + price + recent utilization). - Lower the autoscaler cold-start penalty slightly for cross-region spill to favor availability over cost during short promos. - Fix weight-normalization race when endpoint metadata changes. - Add per-route prefix-cache hit monitoring and integrate with routing decisions.
Ops Lead: Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Luca: Patch routing policy to compute combined_capacity_score and deploy canary in staging — ETA 48h.
- Sam: Tweak autoscaler warmup penalty and run synthetic warmup tests across regions — ETA 72h.
- Maya: Add a dashboard for per-route cache-hit and token accounting; hook alerts at 5% drop — ETA 72h.
- Infra Bot: Run a backfill simulation for promo replay to estimate worst-case spill needs and report — ETA 24h.
- Nora: We'll freeze promo rollout cadence until we validate the new routing policy — FYI.
Luca Patel: Quick mitigation we applied during the incident: temporarily disabled price-ranking and forced round-robin across regions, + lowered per-route concurrency limit to 0.7x for 10 minutes which prevented full cluster OOM but still cost a bit.
Sam O'Neill: Follow-up: we should add a low-latency fallback that returns "busy" early for non-SLA-critical routes to avoid cascading evictions. Could toggle per-customer.
Maya Chen: Good idea. We'll include that as an experiment in the autoscaler change set.
Ops Lead: Postmortem note: classify as "near-oom routing hotspot". Severity: SEV3 (customer latency impact, limited revenue loss). No data exfiltration or sustained OOM.
Maya Chen: Final note — telemetry fixed to add per-route per-AZ GPU headroom metric (will land tomorrow), and I'll follow up with a short retro doc with charts. :speech_balloon: Everyone add anything else before I lock the action items?
Luca Patel: Add unit tests for endpoint weight normalization.
Sam O'Neill: Add a canary traffic generator for price/ranking changes.
Nora (Finance): Please include a cost cap alert for sudden short-term GPU-hour spikes.
Maya Chen: Great — locking this and creating JIRA tasks now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
